reader.requirement: At --std 85, a format 3 SET statement whose operand is the mnemonic-name of an external switch alters that switch's status so that its condition-names then reflect the ON or OFF phrase (§1985:VI.6.23.4 GR6), for every mnemonic-name-1 of each {mnemonic-name-1}... TO {ON|OFF} phrase and every repetition of the phrase; the implementor defines which switches SET may reference, and a mnemonic not associated with such a switch is refused (§1985:VI.6.23.3 SR5).

The path consults the edition nowhere.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness sets one switch TO ON; not exercised: TO OFF, several mnemonics in one phrase, several phrases, a switch whose external status starts ON, a switch with no condition-names, and the SR5 refusals

probes.printed: SET SW1 SW2 TO OFF SW5 TO ON then IF S1-OFF AND S2-OFF -> BOTH-OFF (also with COBOL_SWITCH_1=ON and COBOL_SWITCH_2=on in the environment); SET SW1 TO ON then PERFORM UNTIL S1-OFF with SET SW1 TO OFF at I=3 -> I=3
probes.expected: each named switch takes the phrase's status and its condition-names reflect it (§1985:VI.6.23.4 GR6)

probes.printed: COBOL1757: SET 'OUT-DEV' TO ON - ... 'OUT-DEV' is the mnemonic-name of the device-name 'SYSOUT'
COBOL1757: SET 'SWITCH-1' TO ON - ... 'SWITCH-1' is itself a switch-name, an implementor-name
probes.expected: refused: the operand is the mnemonic-name, not the implementor-name

probes.printed: COBOL1639: SET 'SW1' TO TRUE - 'SW1' is not a condition-name
COBOL0817: DISPLAY UPON 'SW1': 'SW1' is the mnemonic-name of the switch-name 'SWITCH-1', not of a device-name
probes.expected: refused: §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR1, a switch's mnemonic only in SET

reader.notes: SET format 3 binds each mnemonic through the one mnemonic registry and emits ExternalSwitches.Set per switch; every table switch is settable, the implementor's choice documented in DOC-A.1-191. No edition branch on the path.
